title: Move to New Orleans and bands advertising at the corner saloon
summary: The family moves to the corner of Oak and Bordeaux (c. 1915-16); bands stop at the saloon to advertise dances, and young Sayles bangs on tin and wants to play jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Well, it might have been maybe not. I know I was in Donsonville when that storm was. I was... Maybe I might have been 1916. And I did remember we had a severe... We had a heavy snow. We were living in Donsonville. And I got to check on a year with that. What is that, 1916? Because I know right... It was shortly after that. And my father's family came, got a good job in Yarlene. And he moved us all to family. My mother and my sisters and brothers. My father was still living in Yarlene. I mean, he was here already. I mean, we moved everything to... And we lived up on the corner of Oak and Woodhead. And that's where I... Yeah, I went to where I left off. I went to a school called... They call it... It's called St. John of Arts now. But it was called St. Dominic at that time. And there's some particular corner. Like I said, I must have been about eight or nine years old. I remember when on Sunday, especially when the band would go around advertising for the dance that night. They had a saloon right across the street from us on the corner. That was where all the bands would stop and play the advertising. And then they would go in there and the fellow running the place would give them a little drink or refresh them, you know. And see when they were still in that particular corner long, you know. And from that time I always had... Well, I always had... Well, I was inclined from usually from Donovan listening to the Claiborne Williams Band in Donovan Village. And my dad was playing the guitar, you know, and everything. And my dad, I was told, played a little bass. And he also played a viola. And I was told, I used to be picking on a... I used to get me a piece of tin and a stick and used to be beat. And my mother was saying, she sure wish I learned how to play something. So we... So like I said, I've never taken the air and I always got an enthused about jazz and everything, you know. And about the bands in New Orleans. You can cut it.
That's all right. Keep on going. Yeah.

New Orleans. And I always said that I would want to be... I thought to myself, I'd want to be a musician to play in a jazz band. I had because the rhythm of the band and the way the guys played, it really was different from listening to bass bands, brass bands in New Orleans. And of course, Claiborne had an orchestra band, but...
It was different from what now?
